production_rule: Only status=verified is production-ready. review and unverified items require source checking.

questions.question: Which non-Beatle played lead guitar on “While My Guitar Gently Weeps”?
questions.reveal: George Harrison invited Eric Clapton to play on the session.

questions.question: Who sang backing vocals on Peter Gabriel’s “Games Without Frontiers”?
questions.reveal: Kate Bush supplied the backing vocals on Gabriel’s 1980 single.

questions.question: Who mixed the original 1973 release of the Stooges’ Raw Power?
questions.reveal: Iggy Pop produced Raw Power; David Bowie mixed the original release.

sources.label: DavidBowie.com — Raw Power original Bowie mix

questions.question: Which Velvet Underground member came from New York’s avant-garde/minimalist music world?
questions.reveal: John Cale brought viola, drones and an experimental-music background into the Velvet Underground.

questions.question: Who sang the powerhouse guest vocal on the Rolling Stones’ “Gimme Shelter”?
questions.reveal: Merry Clayton’s late-night studio performance became one of rock’s most famous guest vocals.

questions.question: Which future Fleetwood Mac member wrote “Black Magic Woman”?
questions.reveal: Peter Green wrote and recorded the song with Fleetwood Mac before Santana’s hit version.

questions.question: Who played electric piano on the Beatles’ “Get Back”?
questions.reveal: Billy Preston joined the Get Back sessions and was credited on the single.

questions.question: Which artist designed the banana cover for The Velvet Underground & Nico?
questions.reveal: Warhol’s peelable banana became one of rock’s most recognizable sleeves.

questions.question: Before Crosby, Stills & Nash, Graham Nash was in which band?
questions.reveal: Nash left the Hollies in 1968 and joined David Crosby and Stephen Stills.

questions.question: Which producer is synonymous with the “Wall of Sound”?
questions.reveal: Spector’s dense, layered productions defined the Wall of Sound.

questions.question: What does Rush’s title “YYZ” refer to?
questions.reveal: YYZ is the IATA airport code for Toronto Pearson, near Rush’s home city.

questions.question: Which Rush song opens with a rhythm based on the letters YYZ in Morse code?
questions.reveal: The opening rhythm spells Y-Y-Z using Morse-code timing.

questions.question: Who wrote “These Days,” recorded by Nico on Chelsea Girl?
questions.reveal: Jackson Browne wrote “These Days” when he was remarkably young; Nico recorded it for Chelsea Girl.

questions.question: Who co-wrote “Me and Bobby McGee” with Fred Foster?
questions.reveal: Kris Kristofferson and producer Fred Foster wrote the song before Janis Joplin’s famous version.

questions.question: Coolio’s “Gangsta’s Paradise” reworks which Stevie Wonder song?
questions.reveal: The track is built around Stevie Wonder’s “Pastime Paradise” from Songs in the Key of Life.

questions.question: John Williams has said the music in Close Encounters of the Third Kind was influenced by which Disney song?
choices: When You Wish Upon a Star
A Dream Is a Wish Your Heart Makes
The Second Star to the Right
questions.answer: When You Wish Upon a Star
questions.reveal: The Pinocchio song is part of the musical DNA surrounding Close Encounters.

questions.question: Which Police song includes an early pop-culture reference to a VCR?
choices: De Do Do Do, De Da Da Da
When the World Is Running Down, You Make the Best of What’s Still Around
questions.answer: When the World Is Running Down, You Make the Best of What’s Still Around
questions.reveal: The lyric mentions a VCR; the stronger claim that it was the first song to do so still needs verification.
questions.editorial_note: Do not include in production pool until the specific claim and wording are independently verified.

questions.question: Which Suzanne Vega recording became important in the development of MP3 audio compression?
questions.reveal: Vega’s a cappella vocal was repeatedly used as a demanding test signal during MP3 development.

questions.question: What was David Bowie’s birth surname?
questions.reveal: David Robert Jones adopted Bowie as a stage name.

questions.question: Who replaced Eric Clapton in the Yardbirds?
questions.reveal: Jeff Beck followed Clapton; Jimmy Page joined later.

questions.question: Who produced the Velvet Underground’s album Loaded?
questions.reveal: Loaded moved the band toward a more direct, song-oriented sound.

questions.question: Which producer worked on Bob Dylan’s “Like a Rolling Stone”?
questions.reveal: Tom Wilson produced the session that yielded Dylan’s breakthrough electric single.

questions.question: Who played organ on Bob Dylan’s “Like a Rolling Stone”?
questions.reveal: Al Kooper, not originally booked as the organist, slipped onto the instrument and created the signature part.

questions.question: Which guitarist played on Dylan’s “Maggie’s Farm” at Newport in 1965?
questions.reveal: Bloomfield was part of the electric band behind Dylan’s famous Newport set.

questions.question: Which singer wrote “Woodstock” despite not attending the festival?
questions.reveal: Mitchell wrote the song from afar after missing Woodstock; CSNY made it a rock anthem.

questions.question: Which member of CSNY wrote “Ohio”?
questions.reveal: Neil Young wrote “Ohio” in response to the Kent State shootings.

questions.question: Who played the guitar solo on Michael Jackson’s “Beat It”?
questions.reveal: Eddie Van Halen supplied the famous solo while Steve Lukather also played guitar on the track.

questions.question: Who played the guitar solo on Steely Dan’s “Reelin’ in the Years”?
questions.reveal: Session guitarist Elliott Randall played the celebrated solo.

questions.question: Who played fretless bass on Paul Simon’s “You Can Call Me Al”?
questions.reveal: South African bassist Bakithi Kumalo played the track’s remarkable bass part.

questions.question: Which Beatle played drums on the Beatles recording of “Back in the U.S.S.R.” after Ringo temporarily quit?
questions.reveal: With Ringo temporarily absent, the remaining Beatles contributed drums; McCartney is prominently associated with the part.

questions.question: Who played the famous saxophone solo on Gerry Rafferty’s “Baker Street”?
questions.reveal: Raphael Ravenscroft played the instantly recognizable saxophone line.

questions.question: Who played saxophone on the Rolling Stones’ “Brown Sugar”?
questions.reveal: Bobby Keys became a recurring Stones collaborator and played the song’s sax solo.

questions.question: Which singer appears on Massive Attack’s “Teardrop”?
questions.reveal: Cocteau Twins singer Elizabeth Fraser supplied the lead vocal.

questions.question: Who sang lead on the Temptations’ “My Girl”?
questions.reveal: David Ruffin’s lead vocal helped turn “My Girl” into a Motown standard.

questions.question: Who co-wrote the Monkees’ “I’m a Believer”?
questions.reveal: Neil Diamond wrote the song before the Monkees made it a huge hit.

questions.question: Who wrote “Different Drum,” made famous by the Stone Poneys with Linda Ronstadt?
questions.reveal: Monkee Michael Nesmith wrote “Different Drum.”

questions.question: Which future member of the Eagles played with Linda Ronstadt before the Eagles formed?
questions.reveal: Don Henley and Glenn Frey both backed Ronstadt before forming the Eagles.

questions.question: Which singer was originally asked to duet on Peter Gabriel’s “Don’t Give Up” before Kate Bush?
questions.reveal: Gabriel initially had Dolly Parton in mind; Kate Bush ultimately delivered the duet vocal.

questions.question: Which guitarist played the solo on David Bowie’s “Let’s Dance”?
questions.reveal: Stevie Ray Vaughan’s guitar became a defining sound on Bowie’s Let’s Dance album.

questions.question: Who produced David Bowie’s Let’s Dance?
questions.reveal: Chic’s Nile Rodgers produced Bowie’s blockbuster 1983 album.

questions.question: Who played lead guitar on David Bowie’s “Heroes”?
questions.reveal: King Crimson guitarist Robert Fripp created the sustained guitar lines.

questions.question: Which producer collaborated with Bowie on Low and “Heroes”?
questions.reveal: Tony Visconti produced the Berlin-era albums with Bowie; Brian Eno was a crucial collaborator but not the producer.

questions.question: Who produced Joy Division’s Unknown Pleasures?
questions.reveal: Martin Hannett’s spacious, unconventional production became inseparable from Joy Division’s sound.

questions.question: Which graphic designer created the iconic Unknown Pleasures cover treatment?
questions.reveal: Peter Saville adapted the pulsar visualization into Factory Records’ stark sleeve design.

questions.question: Which designer created the Sex Pistols’ ransom-note visual identity?
questions.reveal: Jamie Reid’s cut-and-paste graphics became one of punk’s defining visual languages.

questions.question: Which artist designed the Rolling Stones’ Sticky Fingers cover?
questions.reveal: Warhol conceived the famous jeans-and-zipper package.

questions.question: Who designed the Beatles’ Sgt. Pepper cover with Jann Haworth?
questions.reveal: Peter Blake and Jann Haworth created the famous crowd collage.

questions.question: Which artist designed the Beatles’ White Album packaging?
questions.reveal: Richard Hamilton pushed in the opposite direction from Sgt. Pepper with an almost blank sleeve.

questions.question: Which design studio is strongly associated with classic Pink Floyd album covers?
questions.reveal: Hipgnosis, founded by Storm Thorgerson and Aubrey Powell, created many landmark Pink Floyd sleeves.

questions.question: Which Pink Floyd album cover famously shows a prism dispersing light?
choices: The Dark Side of the Moon
questions.answer: The Dark Side of the Moon
questions.reveal: Hipgnosis and George Hardie created the prism design.

questions.question: Who sang lead on Jefferson Airplane’s “Somebody to Love”?
questions.reveal: Grace Slick brought the song from her earlier band, the Great Society, to Jefferson Airplane.

questions.question: Which band first recorded “Somebody to Love” before Jefferson Airplane?
choices: Big Brother and the Holding Company
questions.reveal: Grace Slick’s Great Society recorded the song before Jefferson Airplane’s hit version.

questions.question: Who wrote Jefferson Airplane’s “Somebody to Love”?
questions.reveal: Grace Slick’s brother-in-law Darby Slick wrote the song.

questions.question: Which band did Janis Joplin front before her solo career?
choices: Big Brother and the Holding Company
questions.answer: Big Brother and the Holding Company
questions.reveal: Joplin’s breakthrough came with Big Brother and the Holding Company.

questions.question: Who designed the cover art for Big Brother and the Holding Company’s Cheap Thrills?
questions.reveal: Underground cartoonist Robert Crumb drew the comic-strip cover.

questions.question: Which producer worked with the Doors on their classic early albums?
questions.reveal: Paul A. Rothchild produced the Doors’ first five studio albums.

questions.question: Who played bass on many Doors studio recordings despite the band having no regular bassist onstage?
questions.reveal: Session musicians augmented the Doors in the studio; Larry Knechtel played bass on parts of the debut.

questions.question: Which Wrecking Crew bassist played on countless Los Angeles pop sessions?
questions.reveal: Carol Kaye became one of the most prolific session bassists of the era.

questions.question: Which drummer was a key member of the Wrecking Crew and later recorded with John Lennon?
questions.reveal: Hal Blaine’s session credits span an extraordinary range of 1960s and 1970s hits.

questions.question: Which bassist is most associated with Motown’s Funk Brothers and lines like “My Girl”?
questions.reveal: James Jamerson transformed electric bass playing from inside Motown’s house band.

questions.question: What was the name of Motown’s studio band?
questions.reveal: The Funk Brothers played on a huge share of Motown’s classic recordings.

questions.question: What was the nickname for the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section?
questions.reveal: The Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section became known as the Swampers.

questions.question: Which singer recorded “Respect” before Aretha Franklin?
questions.reveal: Otis Redding wrote and released “Respect”; Franklin radically transformed it in 1967.

questions.question: Who wrote “Piece of My Heart,” first recorded by Erma Franklin?
questions.reveal: Erma Franklin recorded the song before Big Brother and Janis Joplin made it a rock staple.

questions.question: Which singer first released “Hound Dog” before Elvis Presley?
questions.reveal: Big Mama Thornton’s original recording preceded Elvis Presley’s version by several years.

questions.question: Who wrote “Hound Dog”?
questions.reveal: Leiber and Stoller wrote the song for Big Mama Thornton.

questions.question: Which songwriter wrote “Nothing Compares 2 U”?
questions.reveal: Prince wrote the song; the Family recorded it before Sinéad O’Connor’s global hit.

questions.question: Which band originally recorded “Tainted Love”?
questions.reveal: Gloria Jones first recorded “Tainted Love”; Soft Cell’s synth-pop cover became the international hit.

questions.question: Who wrote “I Love Rock ’n Roll” before Joan Jett made it famous?
questions.reveal: The Arrows first recorded the song; Joan Jett later turned it into a massive hit.

questions.question: Which band first released “The Man Who Sold the World” as a hit cover in 1974?
questions.reveal: Lulu recorded Bowie’s song with Bowie involved in the session and production.

questions.question: Who wrote Mott the Hoople’s “All the Young Dudes”?
questions.reveal: Bowie gave Mott the Hoople the song as the band was considering breaking up.

questions.question: Which Bowie song did Mott the Hoople reportedly turn down before receiving “All the Young Dudes”?
questions.reveal: Bowie first offered another Ziggy-era song before writing/giving them “All the Young Dudes.”

questions.question: Which producer made T. Rex’s classic glam-era records with Marc Bolan?
questions.reveal: Tony Visconti produced T. Rex during their defining glam-rock run.

questions.question: Who produced Queen’s A Night at the Opera with the band?
questions.reveal: Roy Thomas Baker co-produced Queen’s elaborate breakthrough album.

questions.question: Which Queen song famously contains no synthesizers despite its huge layered sound?
questions.reveal: The dense arrangement was built from voices, guitars, piano, bass and drums rather than synths.

questions.question: Who produced the Cars’ debut album?
questions.reveal: Roy Thomas Baker brought his polished, layered production approach to The Cars.

questions.question: Which producer made the Ramones’ End of the Century?
questions.reveal: The pairing of the Ramones with Wall-of-Sound architect Phil Spector was famously combustible.

questions.question: Who produced Patti Smith’s Horses?
questions.reveal: Velvet Underground alumnus John Cale produced Smith’s landmark debut.

questions.question: Who produced the Modern Lovers’ original recordings later compiled as their debut album?
questions.reveal: John Cale produced key early Modern Lovers sessions.

questions.question: Which former Velvet Underground member produced the Stooges’ debut album?
questions.reveal: John Cale produced The Stooges, linking two foundational proto-punk worlds.

questions.question: Which musician produced the first Nico solo album Chelsea Girl?
questions.reveal: Tom Wilson produced Chelsea Girl; its ornate overdubs were famously not to Nico’s taste.

questions.question: Which Velvet Underground album was produced by Tom Wilson?
questions.reveal: Tom Wilson is credited as producer of the band’s abrasive second album.

questions.question: Which producer recorded the Velvet Underground’s early sessions and also worked with Bob Dylan?
questions.reveal: Tom Wilson’s career connects Dylan, Simon & Garfunkel, Frank Zappa and the Velvet Underground.

questions.question: Which Simon & Garfunkel song became a hit after producer Tom Wilson added electric instruments without the duo present?
questions.reveal: Wilson overdubbed electric backing onto the acoustic recording, helping turn it into a hit.

questions.question: Who played drums on the Byrds’ hit recording of “Mr. Tambourine Man”?
questions.reveal: Most of the instrumental backing on the hit single was played by Los Angeles session musicians.

questions.question: Which Byrd played 12-string guitar on “Mr. Tambourine Man”?
questions.reveal: McGuinn’s Rickenbacker 12-string supplied the record’s defining jangle.

questions.question: Who wrote the Byrds’ “Eight Miles High” with Gene Clark and David Crosby?
questions.reveal: The song is credited to Gene Clark, Jim McGuinn (later Roger), and David Crosby.

questions.question: Which jazz musician strongly influenced the guitar approach on “Eight Miles High”?
questions.reveal: McGuinn has cited Coltrane as a key influence on the song’s spiraling guitar language.

questions.question: Which country-rock pioneer joined the Byrds for Sweetheart of the Rodeo?
questions.reveal: Gram Parsons helped push the Byrds decisively toward country music.

questions.question: What band did Gram Parsons form with Chris Hillman after leaving the Byrds?
choices: New Riders of the Purple Sage
questions.reveal: Parsons and Hillman carried their country-rock ideas into the Flying Burrito Brothers.

questions.question: Who sang harmony with Gram Parsons on his solo albums GP and Grievous Angel?
questions.reveal: Parsons helped introduce Emmylou Harris to a wider rock audience through their duets.

questions.question: Which guitarist played with John Mayall’s Bluesbreakers before forming Fleetwood Mac?
questions.reveal: Peter Green followed Eric Clapton through Mayall’s band before forming Fleetwood Mac.

questions.question: Which Fleetwood Mac founder wrote the instrumental “Albatross”?
questions.reveal: Peter Green wrote Fleetwood Mac’s dreamy instrumental chart-topper.

questions.question: Which Fleetwood Mac song later inspired part of the Beatles’ “Sun King” sound, according to George Harrison?
questions.reveal: Harrison explicitly connected the languid guitar atmosphere of “Sun King” to Fleetwood Mac’s “Albatross.”

questions.question: Who played the famous guitar solo on the Carpenters’ “Goodbye to Love”?
questions.reveal: Tony Peluso’s fuzz-guitar solo was startlingly heavy for a Carpenters single.

questions.question: Which guitarist played the solo on Christopher Cross’s “Ride Like the Wind”?
questions.reveal: Larry Carlton supplied the guitar solo on the recording.

questions.question: Which guitarist played the solo on Steely Dan’s “Peg”?
questions.reveal: After multiple players tried the part, Jay Graydon’s solo made the final record.

questions.question: Which drummer played the famous half-time shuffle on Steely Dan’s “Home at Last”?
questions.reveal: Bernard Purdie’s groove is a classic example of the Purdie shuffle.

questions.question: Which drummer played on Paul Simon’s “50 Ways to Leave Your Lover”?
questions.reveal: Steve Gadd created the instantly recognizable military-flavored drum pattern.

questions.question: Who played drums on Toto’s “Rosanna”?
questions.reveal: Jeff Porcaro’s groove blended shuffle influences into one of pop’s most studied drum parts.
